title: H3Match: A Hybrid Heterogeneous Hypergraph Matching Method for Subcircuit Identification
problem: Subcircuit matching in circuit synthesis and verification is slow and inaccurate using prior GNN-based filtering that produces high false negatives and redundant circuit representations.
motivation: Accurate and efficient subcircuit matching is critical for logic synthesis, design verification, and hardware security in large circuit designs.
method: Circuits are represented as heterogeneous hypergraphs (network models with different types of connections). The method uses directed graph neural networks to quickly find approximate circuit matches while reformulating the problem as a directed acyclic graph to reduce missed matches. These approximate results then serve as starting points for an optimization solver (MINLP—mixed-integer nonlinear programming), which finds exact matches faster because it starts with a candidate solution rather than from scratch.
key_novelty: Hypergraph-based circuit representation with directed graph neural networks that reformulate the matching problem as directed acyclic graphs while embedding circular structures to reduce missed matches.
contributions: Heterogeneous hypergraph modeling of circuits capturing rich topology and structural information
Directed GNN-based approximate matching with near-zero false negatives
MINLP formulation for exact verification with 4.16× speedup over prior methods
End-to-end flow achieving 7.08× overall speedup with improved accuracy
limitations: Limited to subcircuit matching scope; performance on very large circuits (>10M gates) not discussed.
primary_theme: Hypergraph GNN for subcircuit matching with low false negatives
